subject: physics
question_text: Explain surface tension and surface energy.

mark_split.label: The two units are the same unit

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Short Answer Question 11 (printed p.110). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: surface tension T = F/l (unit N m⁻¹) is the force per unit length on a line in the liquid surface; surface energy per unit area is W/ΔA = T (unit J m⁻²), from the work W = T × ΔA needed to enlarge the surface by ΔA; reducing J m⁻² to base units gives N·m·m⁻² = N m⁻¹, so the two units are identical and T and surface energy are numerically equal.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Surface tension — the definition
lines: Surface tension is the force acting
per unit length on an imaginary line
drawn in the liquid surface, acting
tangential to the surface:
SI unit newton per metre, N m⁻¹.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Definition, with the unit N m⁻¹.
steps.why: The force alone is not fixed for a liquid — a longer line carries a larger force — so dividing by the length is what makes T a property of the liquid itself.
common_mistakes: Calling surface tension a force. It is a force per unit length.
Giving the unit as newton alone, leaving out the per metre.

recall.must_convey: That surface tension is the force per unit length on a line in the liquid surface, T = F/l, unit N m⁻¹.
reject: work done per unit area increase

steps.memory_tip: Surface tension is force divided by length, not force alone.

steps.label: Surface energy — the definition
steps.mark_note: W = T × ΔA, unit J m⁻²
lines: Surface energy is the work done in
increasing the area of the liquid
surface by one unit:
so the surface energy per unit area
is W/ΔA, unit joule per square
metre, J m⁻².
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Definition, with the unit J m⁻².
steps.why: Enlarging a liquid surface needs work done against the surface tension, so the energy stored is set by how much the area has grown, ΔA.
common_mistakes: Calling surface energy the total energy of the liquid. It is defined per unit increase in area.
Giving the unit as joule alone, leaving out the per square metre.

recall.must_convey: That surface energy is the work done per unit increase in area, W/ΔA, unit J m⁻².
accept: work done per unit area increase
W equals T into delta A

steps.memory_tip: Surface energy is work divided by the extra area, not the total energy.

steps.label: The two units are the same unit
steps.mark_note: N m⁻¹ reduces to J m⁻²
lines: Reduce the surface energy unit to
base terms:

lines.text: J m⁻² = N·m / m² = N m⁻¹

lines: since one joule is one newton
metre. So newton per metre and
joule per square metre are the
same unit, written two ways.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Reduce J m⁻² to N m⁻¹ to show the units match.
steps.why: Two quantities that reduce to the identical unit cannot be independent physical quantities — the unit algebra is the proof that T and surface energy are the same quantity.
common_mistakes: Stopping at N·m/m² without reducing it the final step to N m⁻¹.
Treating the match as a coincidence rather than a consequence of W = T × ΔA.

recall.must_convey: That reducing J m⁻² to base units gives N m⁻¹, so the two units are identical.
accept: J per m squared reduces to N per m
one joule is one newton metre
the two units are the same unit
reject: work done per unit area increase

steps.memory_tip: One joule is one newton metre, so J/m² reduces to N/m.

steps.label: Numerically equal, one property
steps.mark_note: T and the surface energy are the same T
lines: From W = T × ΔA, the surface energy
per unit area works out to T itself.
So surface tension and surface
energy are numerically equal, and
are two descriptions of the one
property of the liquid surface, not
two separate quantities.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. State plainly: numerically equal, one property described two ways.
steps.why: The same symbol T measures the force per unit length and the energy per unit area because one defines the other through W = T × ΔA.
common_mistakes: Calling surface tension and surface energy two different properties that happen to share a value.
Leaving out the word numerically, so the statement reads as if the two quantities were identical in every respect, not only in value.

recall.must_convey: That surface tension and surface energy are numerically equal, being two descriptions of the same property.
accept: two names for the same property
T equals the surface energy per unit area
reject: J per m squared reduces to N per m

steps.memory_tip: One property, two names: force per length and energy per area, same T.

insider_note: The third mark is the one students skip — reducing J m⁻² to N m⁻¹ is what proves the equality, not just stating it.
